config._comment: Simulated-learner necessity test (cdlp/validation/necessity_test.py). gap = control score - score without A. n_questions defaults to 3; compare 2 vs 3 for stability before relying on it. Thresholds are a first, uncalibrated choice: with 3 questions graded in 0.5 steps every gap is a multiple of 1/6, so 0.15 / 0.3 / 0.5 separate one, two and three-or-more half-steps. Calibrate on a held-out split, never on the evaluation gold. Control C: an unrelated in-course concept, else a concept from the other course (cross_course_concepts, keyed by the course being tested), else control_placeholder. question_format 'mcq' grades by exact match with no grader call. with_a_diagnostic adds the 'with A' run (not part of the gap).

control_placeholder.name: Origami Folding
control_placeholder.description: Folding a single sheet of paper into shapes without cutting it.

cross_course_concepts._comment: Fallback controls: concepts of the OTHER course, keyed by the course under test.

questions.question: What is a binary search tree?
options: A binary tree in which values smaller than the root are stored in the left subtree and larger values in the right subtree.
A binary tree in which all values are stored in the right subtree.
A binary tree in which values are stored randomly in the left and right subtrees.
A binary tree in which all values are stored in the left subtree.
questions.reference_answer: A binary tree in which values smaller than the root are stored in the left subtree and larger values in the right subtree.

questions.question: How does a binary search tree store values?
options: Values smaller than the root are stored in the left subtree and larger values in the right subtree.
Values are stored in a circular pattern around the root.
Values are stored randomly in the left and right subtrees.
Values smaller than the root are stored in the right subtree and larger values in the left subtree.
questions.reference_answer: Values smaller than the root are stored in the left subtree and larger values in the right subtree.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a binary search tree?
options: To store values in a way that allows for efficient searching, insertion, and deletion.
To store values in a way that allows for efficient sorting.
To store values in a way that allows for efficient encryption.
To store values in a way that allows for efficient compression.
questions.reference_answer: To store values in a way that allows for efficient searching, insertion, and deletion.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of a binary tree?
options: Each node has at most two children
Each node has at most one child
Each node has no children
Each node has at most three children
questions.reference_answer: Each node has at most two children

questions.question: How are traversals defined in a binary tree?
options: They are defined randomly
They are defined by the user
They are defined recursively
They are defined iteratively

questions.question: What is a possible structure of a node in a binary tree?
options: A node can have at most two children
A node can have any number of children
A node can have no children
A node can have at most one child
questions.reference_answer: A node can have at most two children

questions.question: What is an AVL tree?
options: A type of binary tree used for sorting
A type of hash table
A self-balancing binary search tree
A data structure used for graph algorithms

questions.question: What happens after each insert in an AVL tree?
options: The tree is not rebalanced, but the BST ordering is preserved
The tree is rebalanced, but the BST ordering is not affected
The tree is rebalanced, but the BST ordering is not preserved
The tree is rebalanced and the BST ordering is preserved
questions.reference_answer: The tree is rebalanced and the BST ordering is preserved

questions.question: What is the purpose of rotations in an AVL tree?
options: To balance the tree, but only for certain types of data
To balance the tree and preserve the BST ordering
To unbalance the tree and break the BST ordering
To balance the tree, but not preserve the BST ordering
questions.reference_answer: To balance the tree and preserve the BST ordering
